title: Global Semiconductor Sales Increase 35.1% from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026
gist: SIA reported global semiconductor sales of $403.3 billion in Q2 2026, up 35.1% sequentially, with June sales of $134.5 billion up 123.6% year-over-year and 9.7% month-over-month. SIA CEO John Neuffer expects 2026 global chip sales to exceed $1.5 trillion, driven by the Americas, Asia Pacific and China.

insights.claim: Global semiconductor sales reached $403.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026, a 35.1% increase versus Q1 2026, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association's August 6, 2026 release.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: A 35.1% sequential jump is an extreme quarter-on-quarter move for the industry aggregate and sets a very high base for H2 comparisons.
insights.quote: global semiconductor sales were $403.3 billion during the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 35.1% compared to Q1 of 2026

insights.claim: Global chip sales in June 2026 were $134.5 billion, up 123.6% versus June 2025 and 9.7% versus May 2026.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: A 123.6% year-over-year monthly gain implies the sector more than doubled in a year — a level that pressures capacity and pricing across the supply chain.
insights.quote: Global sales were $134.5 billion during the month of June 2026, an increase of 123.6% compared to June 2025 and 9.7% more than sales in May 2026.

insights.claim: The monthly semiconductor sales figures are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics organization and represent a three-month moving average, not a single discrete month.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: Because the series is a three-month moving average, month-to-month swings are smoothed and turning points appear with a lag — do not read single prints as real-time inflections.
insights.quote: Monthly sales are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization and represent a three-month moving average.

insights.claim: SIA president and CEO John Neuffer said global chip sales are expected to exceed $1.5 trillion in 2026, with Q2 substantially outpacing Q1.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: A $1.5 trillion-plus full-year industry gives an explicit top-down anchor for sizing semiconductor equipment, materials and design-tool TAMs in 2026.
insights.quote: Global chip sales are expected to exceed $1.5 trillion in 2026, with Q2 sales substantially outpacing sales in Q1 2026

insights.claim: SIA attributes market growth to strong sales across the Americas, the Asia Pacific region and China, framing it as evidence of broad-based rather than single-region chip demand.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: Broad regional participation reduces the risk that the cycle is a single-geography or single-customer artifact.

insights.claim: June year-over-year sales growth was highly dispersed by region: Americas +160.9%, Asia Pacific/All Other +124.4%, China +112.8%, Europe +75.2% and Japan +39%.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: The Americas' 160.9% versus Japan's 39% marks a four-fold spread in regional growth, pointing to where the demand — likely AI-linked — is actually concentrated.
insights.quote: year-to-year sales in June were up in the Americas (160.9%), Asia Pacific/All Other (124.4%), China (112.8%), Europe (75.2%), and Japan (39%)

insights.claim: Month-to-month June sales rose in every reported region — China +10.4%, Asia Pacific/All Other +9.8%, Americas +9.6%, Japan +8.6% and Europe +7.7% — a much tighter band than the year-over-year figures.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: Uniform 7.7%-10.4% sequential growth across all five regions suggests current momentum is synchronized globally, unlike the divergent annual base effects.
insights.quote: Month-to-month sales in June increased in China (10.4%), Asia Pacific/All Other (9.8%), the Americas (9.6%), Japan (8.6%), and Europe (7.7%).
